persona.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being erased in plain sight to standing in the life you built, with the words to say so.
understanding.core_struggle: A woman who built a CA practice from zero is being told by her mother-in-law that she will leave it after the baby, while her husband stays silent.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt and grief. Krishna tells him that no one else can be the ultimate support here, so Arjuna must become his own ally. The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. This means you have the power to lift yourself up or push yourself down. You can choose to stand by your own worth and not abandon yourself to the quiet erasure others try to place on you.
verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.for_you: Your mother-in-law is handing you a borrowed life, one where you leave your career after the baby and shrink to fit her picture of a daughter-in-law. This verse shows the pattern: you are being asked to live someone else's duty.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is teaching Nidagha how a person who is truly free moves through the world. They do the work that is right in front of them. They look at friend and enemy with the same clear eyes. They are not pulled around by wanting things or pushing them away. Because of this, they do not grieve over what is lost, and they do not crave what is not theirs. When they speak, they say what everyone can agree with, and they speak gently. They also take time to read the true intent of people's hearts.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today, let it loosen. When you sit down to do your accounting work, let your hands move with the same steady focus Ribhu speaks of. Do the work in front of you without letting the noise in your home pull your mind under.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna is explaining the discipline of speech. He says that true austerity of speech means speaking words that do not cause distress, that are truthful, pleasant, and beneficial. It also means regularly studying what is wise. This is not about hiding the truth or being soft. It is about speaking what is real without wounding the one who hears it.
verse.for_you: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.

story.title: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
story.story_hook: In a hall full of the most learned men in the land, one woman stood up twice.
story.summary: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
story.lesson: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

anchor.speaker: Yajnavalkya
anchor.setting: At King Janaka's debate, Kahola asks about the self.
anchor.sanskrit: या ह्येव पुत्रैषणा सा वित्तैषणा या वित्तैषणा सा लोकैषणोभे ह्येते एषणे एव भवतस्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् । बाल्यं च पाण्डित्यं च निर्विद्याथ मुनिरमौनं च मौनं च निर्विद्याथ ब्राह्मणः ।
anchor.line: Wanting children, wanting money, wanting status: it is one desire. Learn, then live with a child's simplicity.
anchor.translation: The desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds; both are just desires. So a wise man, having done with learning, should seek to live like a child. Having done with both childlike simplicity and learning, he becomes a sage; having done with both silence and its absence, he becomes a true knower.
anchor.why: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

story.for_you: Gargi stood up in a hall full of scholars and asked her hard questions. She did not wait for permission. She did not lower her voice. You can stand in your own kitchen and ask the hard questions about your future.

script: You are sitting with a quiet fury right now because you are being erased, and the people around you refuse to see the CA you built from nothing. You built this life with your own hands, and now you are being told it will disappear, while the silence of your husband leaves you standing in the wreckage alone.
On a battlefield, Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt and grief. Krishna looks at him and says that no one else can be the ultimate support here, so Arjuna must become his own ally. Krishna said:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्, आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः.
In plain words: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.

Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt and grief. Krishna tells him that no one else can be the ultimate support here, so Arjuna must become his own ally. The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. This means you have the power to lift yourself up or push yourself down. You can choose to stand by your own worth and not abandon yourself to the quiet erasure others try to place on you.

Today, sit with the truth that your worth was never theirs to grant. When your mother-in-law speaks, or when your husband changes the subject, let the words land on you like rain on stone. They cannot shrink the life you have built. Your part is to stay on your own side, to keep the CA practice, and to let them see what they are refusing to see.
What would it look like to be your own best friend today?

depth.life: You built a practice from nothing and now someone is drawing a smaller picture of you. Your husband stays quiet and you feel erased. The fury is quiet because the ground beneath you keeps shifting.
depth.points: The text says the self is both your friend and your enemy. When you let their smallness define you, you become your own worst enemy. The only thing that can cut your worth smaller is the story you let them write about you.
depth.practice: Sit with the phone in your hand and name one thing you did today that your mother-in-law did not see. Say it out loud to yourself.
depth.question: What would you say to yourself if your husband finally stood beside you?
